I have been growing stevia on these 3 mu for about 8 years now. Before that I grew corn and wheat, but stevia brings better money if the leaf quality is good. Last year I got about 160 kg per mu and the buyer paid 6 yuan per kilogram. This year I want to reach 170 kg per mu if the rain comes right.

I buy my seedlings from the dealer in Anzhai town. I use the chengguang variety — my neighbor Lao Zhang switched to it three years ago and his leaves are bigger and sweeter than the old type, so I followed him. I plant about 8,000 seedlings per mu. The seedlings cost me around 200 yuan per mu, which is a big expense for my family, but using bad seedlings is the fastest way to lose everything.

For fertilizer, I go by what I learned at the village training meeting two years ago and what I see working in the fields around me. I put down 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as basal dressing when I prepare the land. Then I topdress twice: first time I put 25 kg per mu of 15-15-15 plus 10 kg of urea after the seedlings are established, and second time another 15 kg of urea before the fast growth stage in June. In total that is about 18 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 10 kg of potassium per mu. I also spread about 1,000 kg of chicken manure per mu because stevia likes fertile soil, but the chemical fertilizer is what pushes the yield. I know some people say I use too much, but my wife and I talked it over — my son works in Handan and sends some money home, so we can afford the extra 100 yuan. A bad harvest would cost us ten times that.

I till with the rotary tiller. I do not plough deep because stevia roots stay near the surface and the rotary tiller breaks up the soil fine enough. I irrigate from my well using border irrigation between the rows. Last year I irrigated 4 times, but the weather has been drier lately so this year I will do 5 times — planting time, early May, late May, June, and once in July if it does not rain enough. 

For crop protection, I spray pesticides about 7 times in total. Stevia gets aphids badly in this area, and if you do not control them they cover the underside of the leaves. I use herbicide once after transplanting to stop weeds, then insecticide every two to three weeks during summer, and fungicide once or twice if I see leaf spot appearing. I spend about 150 to 200 yuan per mu on chemicals. I hate spending that money, but last year Lao Zhang tried to save on pesticide and the buyer docked him 20% because of aphid damage on the leaves.

My farm is only 3 mu, so every decision connects to money. If I spend more on fertilizer, I have less for pesticide. If I hire labor, I must borrow from my brother. Mostly it is me, my wife, and my father doing the work. I watch what the other five families in my village group do, and I adjust from last year rather than trying anything completely new. Change is risky when you only have 3 mu.
